evidence.description: FIND-001 (round-0) is resolved: CRIT-004's passThreshold now adds an explicit fourth FAIL trigger -- 'OR if the adversary performs NO Tier-3 live/testnet re-attack at all (an outright skip is itself a FAIL, identical in effect to substitution)'. This closes the loophole where a disk-only review that never attempted any live/testnet re-attack could have been marked PASS. The ambiguous 'out of scope' parenthetical at the prior draft's lines 76-77 is also reworded (current lines 83-85): 'Out of scope for THIS sprint's binary pass refers ONLY to reliance on the stale round-3 self-report ... it does NOT place Tier-3 live re-execution itself out of scope.'

Cross-checked CRIT-004's restated REQ-103 binding language against the source spec text verbatim -- the contract's quoted excerpt ('this re-attack MUST be independently executed by the Phase 3 adversary itself...') matches the spec at these exact lines, confirming the contract's fix is a faithful restatement, not a paraphrase drift.

Cross-checked CRIT-004's Gate-item-3 citation against verification-architecture.md verbatim -- 'the round-1 exploit scripts are re-attempted by the adversary itself, live, producing its own new transaction hashes' matches exactly at these lines.

FIND-004 (round-0) is resolved: CRIT-005's description now reads 'PROP-201a-h -- PROP-201i is explicitly EXCLUDED from this criterion's scope, since CRIT-006 exclusively and concretely grades PROP-201i's lazy/fail-open hl_trade query behavior', making CRIT-005/CRIT-006's scopes disjoint. CRIT-006's passThreshold (lines 132-141) was re-read and confirmed to be the sole owner of PROP-201i(a)/(b)/(c).

FIND-003 (round-0) is resolved: CRIT-001's passThreshold now adds item (4), naming the test 'exactly `★GAP 1★ a live holder's lock is NEVER stolen while it's still working past staleMs (heartbeat keeps it alive)`' as a required-present-by-name check, mirroring CRIT-002's treatment of the atomicity test, with an explicit FAIL trigger for the test being 'missing, renamed away, weakened ... or fails on the adversary's own independent re-run'.

Directly read lock.test.mjs and confirmed the test name at line 24 is character-for-character identical to the name now quoted in CRIT-001: '★GAP 1★ a live holder's lock is NEVER stolen while it's still working past staleMs (heartbeat keeps it alive)', spanning lines 24-61 as cited. No hallucinated citation.

No source files were touched by this round's contract fix (only contracts/sprint-1.md and evidence/sprint-1-green-phase.log were edited per the negotiation note). Round-0's implementation_correctness PASS (isLockStale extraction, atomic fs.rename reclaim, applyAndSave's board-lock-only bounded retry, catalog-gate.mjs's pure filter, hl_trade lazy fail-open query) is carried forward unchanged and re-affirmed by spot-reading lock.test.mjs/gig.test.mjs against the current source, with no regressions in test names or assertions found.

FIND-002 (round-0) is resolved: CRIT-004 and CRIT-008's `dimension` frontmatter fields are now both `verification_readiness`, one of the 5 canonical review dimensions this VCSDD process organizes verdicts around (manifest.json's own `reviewDimensions` list). Neither CRIT item carries the previously undefined `regression_safety` label; no downstream aggregator has to invent a mapping.

FIND-005 (round-0) is resolved: the log's narrative now reads 'all 11 gig.test.mjs tests (8 pre-existing + the ★GAP 2★ regression test -- already counted within those 8 -- + 3 new REQ-102 tests = 11 total)'. Directly counted `test(` occurrences in ~/anicca/skills/economy/gig/__tests__/gig.test.mjs: exactly 11 (2x FINDING1, 2x FINDING2/serialization, 3x FINDING3, 1x GAP2, 3x PROP-102a/b/c). The corrected narrative matches the file's actual contents exactly; the prior '12 pre-existing' overcounting claim is gone.

Fresh-eyes check for new contradictions introduced by the FIND-005 text fix: correcting the 12->11 narrative added net lines to the evidence log, which left a small number of OTHER, single-line evidence citations elsewhere in the contract (CRIT-001's 'line 288' and 'lines 309-317'; CRIT-008's 'line 262' for the PROP-302a result) pointing 1 line early -- e.g. CRIT-001's 'line 288' is now a blank line, with the actual 'exported isLockStale' bullet at line 289; CRIT-008's 'line 262' is PROP-301b's result line, with PROP-302a's own result one line down at 263. This is a genuine, verifiable collateral drift of the FIND-005 fix. It is NOT treated as a blocking finding because: (a) it is immaterial to any CRIT item's binary evaluability -- every affected citation still lands within 1 line of the correct, intended content and is trivially discoverable by any adversary reading a few lines of context (as this review did); (b) it does not misdirect to a substantively wrong section, weaken any FAIL condition, or change any pass/fail outcome; (c) the multi-line-range citations most load-bearing for CRIT-002/003/004's substantive claims (e.g. lines 99-105, 106-116, 78-92) were independently verified to correctly and fully capture their described content. Recommendation for a future increment (non-blocking): re-derive the handful of single-line evidence-log citations against the current file before the next contract revision.

FIND-006 (round-0) is resolved: a new 'Execution-Tooling Note (Phase 3 Prerequisite)' section explicitly states that CRIT-002/003/004/006/007's execution-bound acceptance criteria are discharged during Phase 3 by a review agent 'explicitly provisioned with a code-execution tool (Bash/shell) and, for CRIT-004's Tier-3 half, live/testnet chain access', and explicitly closes the loophole: 'it becomes a violation only if a Phase 3 review claims PASS on CRIT-002/003/004/006/007 without actually being equipped with, and using, an execution-capable (and, where required, chain-capable) tool.' This review's own disk-only tooling is now correctly scoped by the contract's own text as expected and non-violating for a contract-negotiation pass.

Re-confirmed the Tier 0/1/2/3 taxonomy this note maps onto is unchanged and that CRIT-004's added FAIL-on-no-attempt trigger (see spec_fidelity evidence above) now makes the contract's own text, not just this note, force genuine Tier-3 discharge in Phase 3.
